stem: What is the gold standard investigation for diagnosing obstructive sleep apnoea in children?
explanation: Polysomnography is the gold standard investigation for diagnosing obstructive sleep apnoea in children because it measures sleep architecture and respiratory events overnight.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a lateral airway X-ray may suggest adenoidal enlargement but does not diagnose obstructive sleep apnoea.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because sleep diaries and actigraphy are more useful for assessing sleep patterns and circadian rhythm problems than airway obstruction.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because polysomnography provides comprehensive overnight assessment of sleep and breathing and is the gold standard test for diagnosing obstructive sleep apnoea in children.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a morning venous gas analysis reflects a point-in-time metabolic state and cannot measure nocturnal apnoeic events.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because overnight pulse oximetry can support suspicion of sleep-disordered breathing but is not the gold standard diagnostic test.

source.hint: This comprehensive test was mentioned as being invented in Australia and provides a detailed view of sleep architecture and respiratory events.
